statement: Let M = 1000000007. For a length-n list s of integers, define s to be valid iff: (1) for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= s[i] <= 6; (2) for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, gcd(s[i], s[i+1]) = 1; (3) for all i,j with 0 <= i < j < n, if s[i] = s[j] then j - i > 2. Let C(n) be the number of valid length-n lists. The function returns a result r such that r is the unique integer with 0 <= r < M and r is congruent to C(n) modulo M.
preconditions: n is an integer satisfying 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: For every n with 1 <= n <= 10000, whenever the function returns a result r, the integer r satisfies 0 <= r < 1000000007.
preconditions: n is an integer satisfying 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: For every n with 1 <= n <= 10000, the function returns a result; it does not fail with Err.
preconditions: n is an integer satisfying 1 <= n <= 10000.

statement: Let C(n) be the number of valid length-n lists as defined in spec_1: lists s with 1 <= s[i] <= 6 for all 0 <= i < n, gcd(s[i],s[i+1])=1 for all 0 <= i < n-1, and s[i]=s[j] with 0 <= i < j < n only when j-i>2. For every n with 1 <= n <= 10000, whenever the function returns a result r, r is congruent to C(n) modulo 1000000007.
preconditions: n is an integer satisfying 1 <= n <= 10000.
